from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "A vector exists independently of its coordinate description.",
            "Think of an arrow as a geometric object.",
            "Changing basis is changing the language of description."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite & Hook: The 'Same' Vector", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], background_line_style={"stroke_color": "#4A4A4A", "stroke_width": 1})
        self.place_in_area(grid, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.add(grid)
        
        vector = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*2 + UP*1.5, color=WHITE, buff=0)
        label_v = MathTex("v", color=WHITE).next_to(vector.get_end(), UP)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(vector), Write(label_v))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Indicate(vector, color=YELLOW))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show coordinate lines fading in to represent "language"
        self.play(FadeIn(grid))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining Basis Vectors", [
            "A basis is a system of independent vectors.",
            "Standard basis vectors define our default grid.",
            "Custom basis vectors tilt and stretch the grid."
        ])

        # Setup standard grid
        grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"stroke_opacity": 0.3})
        self.place_in_area(grid, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.add(grid)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        i_hat = Vector(RIGHT, color="#00FF00")
        j_hat = Vector(UP, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(i_hat, 'D4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(j_hat, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(i_hat), Create(j_hat))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        # Already showing standard vectors
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        b1 = Vector(RIGHT + UP, color="#FF00FF")
        b2 = Vector(-RIGHT + UP, color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(b1, 'D4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(b2, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        dashed_line = DashedLine(i_hat.get_end(), b1.get_end(), color=WHITE)
        dashed_line2 = DashedLine(j_hat.get_end(), b2.get_end(), color=WHITE)
        
        self.play(Create(b1), Create(b2), Create(dashed_line), Create(dashed_line2))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Transition matrix P links different coordinate systems.",
            "P maps new basis back to standard basis.",
            "Standard coordinates equal P times new coordinates.",
            "View vectors as room-centric or claw-centric.",
            "Projection visually maps new components onto standard axes."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Change-of-Basis Matrix", lecture_lines)
        
        # Matrix Setup
        matrix_p = Matrix([["p_{11}", "p_{12}"], ["p_{21}", "p_{22}"]]).set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_p, 'C2', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix_p))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(matrix_p.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        eq = MathTex(r"[v]_{std} = P [v]_{new}").set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(eq, 'E2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(eq))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.play(matrix_p.animate.set_color("#FF00FF"), eq.animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#00FF00")
        # Visual of columns
        col1 = matrix_p.get_columns()[0].copy().set_color("#00FF00")
        self.play(col1.animate.shift(RIGHT * 1.5))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "First, identify your new basis vectors.",
            "Second, build matrix P using those vectors.",
            "Third, multiply P by your coordinate vector.",
            "This maps to standard representation efficiently.",
            "Procedure converts any basis to standard coordinates."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Step-by-Step Calculation Procedure", lecture_lines)
        
        # Prepare Mobjects
        # Representing matrix P and vector V
        P = Matrix([[2, 1], [1, 2]], left_bracket="[", right_bracket="]")
        V = Matrix([[1], [1]], left_bracket="[", right_bracket="]")
        V_prime = Matrix([[3], [3]], left_bracket="[", right_bracket="]")
        
        equation = MathTex("P", " \cdot ", "V", "=", "V'").scale(1.2)
        
        # Positioning
        self.place_at_grid(P, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(V, "B4", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(equation, "D3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Hide initially
        P.set_opacity(0)
        V.set_opacity(0)
        equation.set_opacity(0)
        V_prime.set_opacity(0)

        # Animation flow
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(FadeIn(P))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(FadeIn(V))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(FadeIn(equation))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(equation.copy(), V_prime.set_color(YELLOW)))
        self.play(FadeIn(V_prime))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(Flash(V_prime, color=WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis & Practical Application", [
            "Change of basis simplifies complex linear problems.",
            "Diagonalization becomes easier with the right basis.",
            "The geometric vector object always stays invariant."
        ])
        
        # Define objects
        vec_v = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT*1.5 + UP*1.0, color=BLUE)
        label_v = MathTex(r"\\mathbf{v}", color=BLUE)
        
        basis_orig = VGroup(
            Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT, color=GRAY),
            Arrow(ORIGIN, UP, color=GRAY)
        )
        
        basis_new = VGroup(
            Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT*0.5 + UP*0.8, color=YELLOW),
            Arrow(ORIGIN, -UP*0.8 + RIGHT*0.5, color=YELLOW)
        )

        grid_asset = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg")
        compass_asset = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/compass.svg")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_at_grid(grid_asset, 'C3', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(vec_v, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(label_v, 'B3')
        self.place_at_grid(basis_orig, 'B2')
        self.play(FadeIn(grid_asset), Create(basis_orig), Create(vec_v), Write(label_v))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.place_at_grid(basis_new, 'B2')
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(basis_orig, basis_new))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_at_grid(compass_asset, 'D4', scale_factor=0.3)
        highlight = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#7FFF00").shift(vec_v.get_end())
        self.play(Create(highlight), FadeIn(compass_asset))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#7FFF00")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Change of Basis in Linear Algebra
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students in Mathematics, Engineering, or Computer Science

sections.title: Prerequisite & Hook: The 'Same' Vector
sections.content: Define a vector as a geometric arrow (independent of coordinates). Introduce the idea that while the arrow stays the same, the 'language' (basis) used to describe it can change. Use the analogy of describing a location: '3 miles North, 2 miles East' vs. 'GPS coordinates'.
sections.example: A cat sitting on a 2D floor. Describe its position relative to the corner of the room (Basis A) versus relative to the center of the rug (Basis B).

sections.title: Defining Basis Vectors
sections.content: Explain a basis as a coordinate system defined by linearly independent vectors. Visualize standard basis vectors (e.g., î=[1,0], ĵ=[0,1]) and transform them into custom basis vectors (e.g., b1=[1,1], b2=[-1,1]).
sections.example: Animation: Show the grid lines stretching and rotating from the standard square grid to a skewed, tilted grid.

sections.title: The Change-of-Basis Matrix
sections.content: Introduce the transition matrix (P). Explain that P maps coordinates from the 'New' basis back to the 'Standard' basis. Emphasize the formula: [v]standard = P * [v]new. Show this visually by projecting the new vector components onto the standard axes.
sections.example: Robot Arm: Mapping the position of a robot's claw from its own 'hand-centric' coordinate system to the 'room-centric' coordinate system.

sections.title: Step-by-Step Calculation Procedure
sections.content: Provide a clear 3-step algorithm: 1. Identify the 'New' basis vectors. 2. Construct matrix P by placing basis vectors as columns. 3. Multiply P by the coordinates in the new basis to find the standard representation.
sections.example: Given Basis B = {[2,1], [1,2]}, convert the coordinate vector [1,1]_B into standard coordinates: 1*[2,1] + 1*[1,2] = [3,3].

sections.title: Synthesis & Practical Application
sections.content: Summarize that changing bases allows us to simplify complex problems (like diagonalizing matrices). Highlight that the vector 'object' is invariant; only its 'description' changes.
sections.example: Video Game Physics: Moving a character 'forward' relative to the camera's current perspective versus the world's fixed north direction.
